questions.q: What does "promote the artifact, not rebuild it" mean in a GitOps promotion workflow?
options: The exact same built container image moves unchanged through dev, staging, and prod; only the Git config pointing to its tag changes
Every environment should build its own image from source using the same Dockerfile
Only the staging environment is allowed to run automated tests
The artifact should be deleted from the registry after each environment uses it
questions.explain: The same immutable image (identified by tag or digest) is promoted unchanged between environments; rebuilding per environment risks staging and prod silently being different bytes despite looking identical in Git.

questions.q: What specifically can go wrong if staging and prod each rebuild the application from source instead of promoting the same tag?
options: Nothing — rebuilding is always equivalent to promoting the same artifact
ArgoCD and Flux cannot reconcile rebuilt images at all
A different cached layer, a dependency resolving to a newer patch version, or a build flag left on can make 'it worked in staging' meaningless, since the two builds aren't the same bytes
The Kustomize overlay directories are deleted automatically
questions.explain: Rebuilding per environment reopens the exact class of bug GitOps is meant to close: subtle build differences (cached layers, dependency versions, flags) mean staging's validation no longer proves anything about what prod will actually run.

questions.q: In the promotion workflow described, what does a promotion PR from dev to staging actually change?
options: It rewrites the application's source code to match staging's requirements
It deletes the dev overlay once staging is created
It copies the same image tag from the dev overlay into the staging overlay, ideally as a near one-line diff
It creates a brand-new container image tagged specifically for staging
questions.explain: The promotion PR's diff should show the identical tag moving from dev's overlay into staging's overlay — copied, not re-tagged or rebuilt — which is what keeps the artifact itself unchanged across environments.

questions.q: After ArgoCD or Flux reconciles a promotion to prod, what should you actually check to confirm the rollout succeeded?
options: Only that Sync status shows Synced
Health status, since Sync status only confirms the manifests were applied, not that the workload is actually running well
The number of commits in the Git repository
Whether the staging overlay still contains the old tag
questions.explain: Sync status only means the live state matches Git; Health status is what tells you whether the newly promoted workload is actually functioning, which is the real signal for rollout success.

questions.q: What does rolling back a bad promotion actually involve under this GitOps workflow?
options: Manually running kubectl rollout undo against the production cluster
Rebuilding the previous version's image from source and re-pushing it
Deleting the entire config repo and starting over
Reverting the promotion PR's Git commit, which lets ArgoCD or Flux reconcile the cluster back to the previous known-good tag automatically
questions.explain: Because the promotion was a Git commit changing one tag value, undoing it is a git revert on that commit — ArgoCD/Flux then reconciles the cluster back to the prior state with no manual cluster commands and no guessing which version ran before.
